title: Vaults GB MUSIC TEST (VRUN: Vaults of Obsolete Code's music as a player ROM)
description: The music test spinoff of VRUN: Vaults of Obsolete Code on the Game Boy (project vrun-voc), modelled on CTW NES's AudioPlayer: the game's real music driver (src/music, the same files the game builds), the song list (all 22 tracks of the game: title, levels 1-20, clear) and one FL TEST slot (list 23), nothing else. musictest/build_musictest.ps1 makes the roster (musictest/make_roster.py: the game's tools/music/roster.json + the FL TEST song), converts it with the game's tools/music/convert.py and links the player (musictest/player.c) with the driver; the game's build.ps1 is not touched. An .flp song goes into the FL TEST slot with BrokenDev/tools/music/flp/musictest/build-vaults-gb-mt.ps1 (FruityHost mt-export vocgb: VocGbBackend's events, the game roster's import).

steps.name: build
steps.note: musictest/build_musictest.ps1: make_roster.py + convert.py into build/musictest/gen (FL TEST = the roster's placeholder), lcc -autobank; MBC5 + RAM + battery, 1 MB, dual mode (the user's flash cart).

run.note: The first track plays at power-on. Up / Down a track (held: repeats), A play from the start, B stop, Left / Right a channel (P1 P2 WV NS), Select mute / unmute it, Start solo it (again: no solo). Songs loop. List 23 = FL TEST.

memory.what: the game's driver advances the song

scenarios.why: power-on: the list on screen, the first track sounds

memory.what: all four channels muted from the pad

scenarios.why: mute from the pad changes the output: the four channels muted = silence while the song plays on
the FL TEST slot plays (the placeholder here; an .flp's song with build-vaults-gb-mt.ps1)

knownIssues: The 22 tracks are the game's: today 11 placeholder songs (from the VRUN NES soundtrack); several tracks share one, as in the game.
No effects driver (tests/music/sfx_stub.c sets the sound chip up as the game does); the screen redraw is slow (printf), so held Up / Down repeats about 4 times a second.
The user's songs are written with NES-console BrokenNes2 instances: mt-export reads them as Game Boy instances when a song has none for the Game Boy (a fence note says so).
